egress.terms: Quoted as a hard monthly transfer figure per plan: 4 TB / 12 TB / 18 TB / 24 TB on a 1 Gbps port. So 2-3x storage per month. ServaRICA's separate 'unlimited' offer is a different product line: unlimited transfer starting at 250 Mbps and growing +1 Mbps/day up to 1 Gbps.

interface_detail: KVM/Xen + root, so anything: SFTP, rsync, NFS, rclone serve s3, MinIO, WebDAV via container
tooling: Root access makes this the most chainable option among the storage providers compared: AList, MinIO or a Cloudflare tunnel endpoint can run on the box itself.
chaining: not stated in the seed record; composition with the pool is unestablished
limits_note: Bandwidth is a hard counter on these plans. Capacity grows +1 GB/day on the 'expanding' line. Billing/ordering was offline during my check (see reliability note).
reliability_note: Canadian provider since 2010, RAIDZ2. Two operational negatives observed this session: (1) their unlimited-storage page currently serves "Client area and billing are temporarily offline. We have intentionally taken clients.servarica.com ... down while we patch all of our PHP services following the recent security issues" — an active security incident response; (2) LET users report orders held by an automatic risk check before manual release. Treat as a real but currently-wobbly vendor.
